column3: NSGA-II global search plus Tchebycheff hill-climbing applied to a share of offspring (Lamarckian).
column4: • Better than plain NSGA-II on P5: IGD 0.010 vs 0.013 †.; • Cheap local search: only 35 extra evaluations on P5 †.; • Works for binary (P9) and permutation (P8) problems via swap/flip moves.; • Keeps all NSGA-II advantages (elitism, crowding).; • Local step can repair infeasible designs.
column5: • Extra parameters: p_ls and L (see sensitivity study).; • On P9 only 4 non-dominated subsets and 11.1s for 3,000 evaluations †.; • Local search can reduce diversity if applied too often.; • Random weights bias towards the middle of the front.; • Local steps cost evaluations: 10,035 used on P5 †.
column6: Mixed global/local problems such as P5 and feature selection.
column7: Very expensive evaluations (local steps multiply cost).

column3: Reference vectors partition the objective space; each vector keeps the solution with the smallest angle-penalised distance; vectors adapt to the objective range.
column4: • Strong on M = 5: HV 0.794 (vs NSGA-II 0.131) †.; • Very cheap (0.1s for 10,000 evaluations) †.; • Angle penalty trades convergence against diversity over time.; • Reference-vector adaptation handles scaled objectives.; • No sorting.
column5: • Population shrinks to the number of occupied vectors (50 points on M=3, 40 on M=5) †.; • IGD 0.139 on M=3 is worse than NSGA-III's 0.104 †.; • Needs the budget (t_max) for the penalty schedule.; • α and f_r are extra parameters.; • Designed for regular fronts.
column6: Many-objective problems with a regular front (P10).
column7: Few objectives where simpler methods are enough.

column3: Fitness = −Σexp(−I_ε+(y,x)/(cκ)) from pairwise additive-ε indicators; remove the worst until N remain; no explicit diversity step.
column4: • Simple, no sorting, no density estimator; P14 IGD 0.004 †.; • Fast (0.4s) †.; • Indicator directly encodes the preferred set quality.; • Spread is good: Spacing 0.003 on P14 †.; • Handles any number of objectives.
column5: • Fewer points on P3 (75) with IGD 0.013 †.; • κ must be tuned and the objective scaling matters (min-max of union).; • O(N²M) pairwise indicator matrix each generation.; • Biased toward the knee and boundaries of the ε-indicator.; • P3 Spacing 0.007 is worse than MO-TLBO's 0.006 †.
column6: Preference-free approximation of the front for 2–5 objectives (P14).

column3: Steady-state (μ+1): one child per step; drop the individual with the smallest exclusive hypervolume contribution in the worst front.
column4: • Hypervolume-optimal subsets: HV 0.534 on P3 and 0.700 on P14 †.; • Even spacing (Spacing 0.002 on P14) †.; • No diversity parameter at all.; • Steady-state allows fine control of the budget.; • Theoretical link to HV maximisation.
column5: • Slow in Python: 4.4s for 10,000 iterations †.; • Only 50 points (population size) — 50 on P3 †.; • Exact HV contribution is exponential for M ≥ 4 (needs Monte Carlo).; • Reference point choice affects the result.; • Sequential: hard to parallelise.
column6: 2–3 objectives where hypervolume is the target quality.

column3: Monte-Carlo estimate of hypervolume-based fitness (weights α_j for k individuals to remove); tournament and survival by this fitness.
column4: • Works for many objectives where exact HV is impossible: M=5 HV 0.990 †.; • Large HV on M=3 too (0.695) †.; • Sample count controls the accuracy/time trade-off.; • No diversity parameter.; • Fine-grained fitness for dominated points.
column5: • Noisy fitness; slow (5.6s for 10,000 evaluations at M=5) †.; • IGD 0.383 on M=5 shows HV-optimality ≠ uniform coverage (solutions pushed toward the boundary) †.; • Needs a reference point and sample budget.; • Results vary with the random samples.; • Cost grows with the number of samples × population.
column6: Many-objective problems when HV is the quality measure.

column3: NSGA-II where crowding distance is replaced by the preference rank (distance to the DM reference point) with ε-clearing.
column4: • Concentrates the population near the DM's point: P14 front spans 1.69–1.80 kg vs 1.53–2.13 kg for IBEA †.; • Very even inside the focus (Spacing 0.000 on P5) †.; • Saves evaluations in regions the DM does not care about.; • Several reference points allowed.; • Inherits NSGA-II's elitism.
column5: • If the reference point is badly placed the focus region is wrong (P14 point is a dominated, attainable point) †.; • Worse IGD against the full front on P5 (0.309) – by design †.; • ε must be tuned (too large → no focus, too small → clustering).; • Does not reveal the rest of the front.; • Slower than NSGA-II (3.6s) † because of the Python ε-clearing loop.
column7: Exploratory phase when the DM has no preference yet.
